issues.title: Canonical trun version can mix versions 0 and 1 in a CMAF video track
issues.author: tobbee
issues.body:
## Problem

Canonical Reconstruction sets `trun.version = 1` iff any effective composition-time offset of the chunk is negative, and `0` otherwise. The version is decided chunk by chunk.

CMAF (ISO/IEC 23000-19:2024, 9.2.5) allows a video track one of two forms, not both:

- **(a)** version 1 TrackRunBoxes, with composition offsets that make each fragment's earliest presentation time equal to its `baseMediaDecodeTime` (see also 7.5.17), or
- **(b)** an offset edit list in the CMAF header, with version 0 TrackRunBoxes.

Under the current rule, a video track of form (a) is rebuilt with version 0 in every chunk that has no negative offset. A version 0 chunk with positive offsets and no edit list fits neither form. Short chunks often have no negative offset. For example, at 90 kHz with 3000 ticks per frame:

- a chunk `I P B B` with offsets `0, 9000, -3000, -3000` is rebuilt as version 1;
- the next chunk, a single `P` frame with offset `+3000`, is rebuilt as version 0.

Chunks whose offsets are all zero (no B-frames) also become version 0 next to version 1 chunks. Checkers report this as mixed `trun` versions; dashcheck reports `SEG-CMAF-COMPTIME`.

Timing is not affected. Effective offsets are signed 32-bit values, and a non-negative offset means the same in both versions. Only the version byte of the canonical `trun` differs, but that is enough to make the rebuilt track non-conformant.

This was found by checking the golden vectors with dashcheck (Eyevinn/locmaf#13). The third chunk of `negative-ctos` had no negative offset and was rebuilt as version 0 between version 1 chunks. That PR changes the vector's offsets, but the rule is unchanged.

## Proposed rule

> `trun.version = 1` iff any effective composition-time offset is negative, **or** the track is video (handler `vide`) and its CMAF header has no EditListBox. Otherwise `0`.

- **Video without an edit list:** always version 1 (form a), including chunks whose offsets are all zero.
- **Video with an edit list:** version 0 (form b). A chunk gets version 1 only if it has negative offsets. That breaks CMAF in the source, but version 0 cannot carry negative offsets.
- **Audio, subtitles and metadata:** unchanged.

The rule needs only the CMAF header, which the receiver already has, and changes nothing on the wire.

## Edit list

The rule only checks whether the CMAF header has an EditListBox; it does not look at its entries. In a CMAF header, an edit list can only shift the timeline. CMAF (ISO/IEC 23000-19:2024, 7.5.13) restricts an EditListBox there to a single entry with media rate 1 and `segment_duration` 0, which CMAF calls an offset edit list. So whether one exists is all the rule needs to know.

## Packaging version

The wire format does not change, but the canonical bytes change for most video chunks. Canonical reconstruction is byte-exact, and conformance is checked by comparing bytes. An implementation of the current rule and one of the new rule would therefore disagree, while both claim `locmafVersion` 0.3. It is reasonable to release this as `locmafVersion` 0.4.

## Work

- Draft: the `trun` subsection of Canonical Reconstruction, and `locmafVersion` 0.4.
- Eyevinn/locmaf:
  - `computeLayout` in `reconstruct.go`.
  - The `align` explainer (`conform/normalize.go`), which today says nothing about a `trun` version difference between source and canonical.
  - Regenerate `testdata/vectors`. Every video canonical chunk changes; objects do not.
  - Vector cases for a video chunk without negative offsets, and for a video track with an edit list.
  - The bump to 0.4: `locmaf.Version`, the moqlivemock catalog gate, the msf-catalog-validator CUE pin, and the locmaf.dev version strings.

issues.title: Boxes between moof and mdat: say how a publisher carries them
issues.author: tobbee
issues.body:
## Problem

In the moof-carrying shape, the `mdat` immediately follows the reconstructed `moof`, so that shape cannot represent a box placed between a chunk's `moof` and its `mdat`. The draft does not say what a publisher does with such a chunk.

## Is such a box allowed?

It is outside the CMAF chunk structure, but not forbidden outright:

- ISO/IEC 23000-19:2024, 7.3.2.3 (Table 7): a CMAF chunk is an optional `styp`, `prft` and `emsg`, then `moof`, then `mdat`. Item (c) says the `mdat` *should* (not *shall*) immediately follow the `trun`.
- Where CMAF allows extra boxes (7.3.2.3 NOTE 3, 7.3.2.4 c), they precede a chunk.
- ISO BMFF on its own allows the box: `data_offset` can skip over it.

So the layout is rare and discouraged, but a relay could receive it.

## Proposal

Carry such a chunk verbatim, as a rawBoxes Object holding the whole chunk (`moof`, the boxes, `mdat`). This is the existing "verbatim chunk carriage" use of rawBoxes: it keeps every byte, at plain-CMAF cost. Add the case to that use, and state that such a chunk is never carried in the moof-carrying shape.

Moving the boxes in front of the `moof` as genBoxes would change the chunk's bytes and its `data_offset`. If publishers could choose either encoding, one source would have two encodings, and canonical comparison would no longer be well-defined. The draft avoids that elsewhere for the same reason.

## Implementation status

mp4ff v0.62.0 refuses to parse a fragmented file in which an `mdat` does not immediately follow a `moof` (`does not support free between moof and mdat`). `locmaf pack` and `locmaf align` therefore reject such input instead of losing the boxes. Supporting it needs mp4ff to accept these boxes and attach them to the fragment, and `pack` to emit a rawBoxes Object for such a chunk. Until then, rejecting the input is acceptable.

pulls.title: LOCMAF v0.3: genBox + full/delta header redesign
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
## What

Reworks the draft around a self-delimiting element sequence — zero or more `genBox` elements (any box outside `moof`: `styp`, `prft`, `emsg`, `uuid`, carried verbatim), exactly one full or delta `moof` header, then the raw `mdat` payload — and bumps `locmafVersion` to `"0.3"`.

## Highlights

- **Integer notation**: MOQT vi64 (Section 1.4.1) throughout; signed values as zigzag vi64. Full 32-bit `sample_flags` carried (compact 5-bit form dropped).
- **Canonical CMAF reconstruction** defined as a function of *effective values* (not wire presence), plus a canonical encoding for encode-side golden vectors. `saio` offsets are moof-relative, version 0; reconstructed boxes never need 64-bit sizes. CENC `senc`/`saiz`/`saio` reconstruction cross-checked against ISO/IEC 23001-7:2023 and Bento4.
- **Simpler DRM**: scheme-agnostic (`cbc1`/`cens` carried with explicit IVs); the cenc IV counter-prediction rule is dropped — per-sample IVs are always explicit; `cbcs` (constant IV) remains the only scheme-specific case.
- **Simpler timeline handling**: delta headers never carry an absolute `tfdtBaseMediaDecodeTime`; a BMDT discontinuity re-anchors with a mid-group full header. Parity exceptions drop from four to three.
- **Transport rules**: one subgroup per group, no datagram forwarding, delta state resets on gaps.
- **Catalog**: `locmaf` packaging is signaled in CMSF catalogs only, mirroring `cmaf`, with a conditional `locmafVersion` track field.
- **New informative section**: minimal self-framing for use outside MOQT (vi64 length-prefixed Objects) covering on-disk storage, LL-DASH, and LL-HLS parts.
- Consumption described generically via chunk and frame interfaces; single author, with Hugo Björs credited in the acknowledgments.

pulls.title: Carry the mfhd sequence number with a delta-coded step
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
LOCMAF has so far reconstructed every chunk with `mfhd.sequence_number = 0`. This PR carries the source value instead.

## Why

C2PA live video (2.4, §19.4.1) can use the `mfhd` `sequence_number` as the segment `sequenceNumber`, and the signed segment hash covers the `moof` bytes unless the signer excludes them. A reconstruction that writes 0 can never match such a hash.

## Wire format

- `mfhdSequenceNumber` (ID 18): the absolute value. It appears only in full headers, is sent only when it is not 0, and must not exceed `0xFFFFFFFF`.
- `mfhdSequenceNumberStep` (ID 20): appears only in delta headers and is delta-coded like any scalar field. A full header resets it to 0.
- A delta chunk's number is the previous chunk's number plus the step, modulo 2^32.

Cost for the two common packager patterns:

- Same number in every chunk of a segment (livesim2 `--c2pa`, moqlivemock): nothing beyond the full header.
- +1 per chunk (ffmpeg counts moofs): one two-byte field in the first delta header of each group.

Jumps, decreases and resets are step changes, or a full header. CMAF §7.5.15 allows values that repeat or decrease.

## Versioning

The extensibility rule now separates decoding from canonical bytes. A new field can be added within a version when ignoring it still gives *decode-equivalent* output: the same samples, timing, sample flags and decryption parameters. Only an extension that changes what the samples decode to needs a new `locmafVersion`.

A receiver that skips IDs 18 and 20 writes `sequence_number = 0`. The chunk plays but is not canonical, so `locmafVersion` stays `"0.3"`.

## Other changes

- Header-kind restrictions in the parity section, now four fields.
- Field table, with `mfhd` rows first.
- Full-header emission rule for ID 18.
- Effective values and the canonical `mfhd` rule.
- One canonical-encoding rule: the step changes only through deltas, never through deletion.
- Range checks in Security Considerations.
- Informative reference to the C2PA 2.4 specification.

The implementations (`Eyevinn/locmaf`, moqlivemock, warp-player) still write 0 and will follow separately.

pulls.title: Cite MOQT -23, LOC -05 and the current ISO editions
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Updates the references to the latest published versions and fixes two wrong CMAF clause numbers.

## IETF drafts

- **MOQT -18 → -23.** The vi64 encoding is unchanged but moved from Section 1.4.1 to Section 8.1, so the citation now points there. -23 renames Forwarding Preference to Delivery Mode, so the ban on Datagram delivery now reads "MUST NOT use the Datagram Delivery Mode".
- **LOC -02 → -05.** Section 2.3 still defines the even/odd property scheme that LOCMAF reuses.
- **MSF and CMSF** stay at -01, still the latest published versions.

## ISO standards

- **ISO BMFF:** 14496-12:2024 → 14496-12:2026. The cited clauses 8.8.3.1 and 8.8.5 are unchanged.
- **CENC:** 23001-7:2024 → 23001-7:2023. There is no 2024 edition; the 4th edition from 2023 is current, and the cited clauses 7.1 and 10.4 match it.
- **CMAF:** 23000-19:2024 is still current. Two clause numbers pointed at the wrong definitions:
  - "CMAF fragment": §7.3.2.2 (the CMAF track) → §7.3.2.4.
  - "CMAF segment": §7.3.2.4 (the CMAF fragment) → §7.3.3.1.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

pulls.title: Signal the LOCMAF version as a packagingMetadata key
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Replaces the separate `locmafVersion` catalog field with a `version` key in the MSF `packagingMetadata` track field.

## Why

The MSF editor's copy adds a `packagingMetadata` track field (moq-wg/msf#211, merged 2026-11-02). It holds `key=value` pairs separated by `;`, and the specification for the track's packaging value defines the keys. That is the job `locmafVersion` did, so a `locmaf` track entry now carries:

```json
"packaging": "locmaf",
"packagingMetadata": "version=0.3"
```

LOCMAF then adds no catalog field of its own, and CMSF only has to register the `locmaf` packaging value.

## What carries over

- The `version` key is required on a `locmaf` track.
- A receiver must not subscribe to a track whose `version` it does not support, or whose `packagingMetadata` has no `version` key. It may pick an alternative packaging of the same source instead.
- MSF requires receivers to ignore keys that are not defined for the packaging value, so later LOCMAF versions can add keys.

The other mentions of `locmafVersion` (the extensibility rule, the catalog summary, and the note on DASH/HLS carriage) now say "LOCMAF packaging version".

## Before merging

`packagingMetadata` is not in the published MSF -01, only in the editor's copy. The MSF reference is now -02, so this should merge once MSF -02 is published. Until then the rendered draft shows a placeholder entry for that reference.

## Follow-ups

- moq-wg/cmsf#27 now uses `packagingMetadata` instead of its `locmafVersion` field.
- #6 cites CMSF -02, which registers the `locmaf` packaging value (moq-wg/cmsf#27), and drops the registration from this draft.
- Implementations switch from `locmafVersion` to `packagingMetadata`: the moqlivemock catalog gate, warp-player, the msf-catalog-validator CUE schema, and the version strings on locmaf.dev.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

pulls.title: Add Related Work on ROHC and the low-overhead HEIF format
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Adds a short informative Related Work subsection (1.1) at the end of the Introduction. It places LOCMAF next to two earlier designs.

## What it says

- **ROHC (RFC 3095, RFC 5795):** the IETF precedent for LOCMAF's delta headers. Compressor and decompressor each keep a context, which packets carrying complete headers initialize, and later headers are sent relative to it. Because link packets can be lost or damaged, ROHC checks decompressed headers with CRCs. It repairs the context through feedback in the bidirectional modes, or through periodic refreshes in U-mode. LOCMAF instead ties its reference to a MOQT group, sent in order on one subgroup stream. A full chunk at the start of the group, or a later one, sets the reference much like a ROHC refresh. After a gap, the receiver resumes at the next full chunk or group.
- **Low-overhead HEIF (ISO/IEC 23008-12:2025/Amd 2:2026):** the MPEG precedent for a compact form that the receiver expands into standard ISO BMFF boxes. A single `mini` box replaces `meta` + `mdat` for one still image, much as a LOCMAF receiver expands an Object into a CMAF chunk. It covers one standalone image only, so it has no delta coding.

Three informative references are added: `RFC3095`, `RFC5795` and `HEIF-AMD2`. There are no normative changes.

## Why

Both techniques LOCMAF uses, delta coding against a shared reference and a compact form with a defined expansion, have published precedents. Naming them helps reviewers place the design. It also shows that LOCMAF's delta coding within a group is the part neither precedent covers.

For context, measured with libheif 1.23.7 (`heif-enc --mini`): `mini` saves a constant ~234 bytes per file. For a 128×128 AVIF, container overhead drops from 270 to 35 bytes. That fits keeping CMAF Header compression out of scope, since LOCMAF sends the CMAF Header once per subscription, not once per Object.

## Review notes

- The ROHC paragraph has been checked against RFC 3095: IR state (§4.3.1.1), LSB/W-LSB encoding (§4.5.1–4.5.2), modes (§4.4), residual errors and CRCs (§4.6), U-mode periodic refreshes (§5.3.1.1.2), and the context and context repair definitions (§2).
- `make`, `make lint` and the 72-column check pass.

pulls.title: Cite CMSF -02, which registers the locmaf packaging value
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Follows #4. Counterpart of the CMSF PR moq-wg/cmsf#27 (https://github.com/moq-wg/cmsf/pull/27), which registers `locmaf` among the MSF packaging values in CMSF and references this draft. Once that is in CMSF -02, this draft no longer needs to register the value itself.

## What changes

- Cites CMSF -02 instead of -01.
- Catalog Signaling drops this draft's own registration table for `locmaf` and the note that the value would migrate into CMSF once CMSF registers it. The section now says that CMSF registers `"locmaf"` next to `"cmaf"` and references this document for the Object encoding.

The rest of the section is unchanged: a track carrying LOCMAF media declares `"packaging": "locmaf"`, and `locmaf` is defined for CMSF catalogs only.

## Before merging

CMSF -02 is not published yet. It needs to include moq-wg/cmsf#27, which adds the `locmaf` registration and is approved but not merged. Until CMSF -02 is posted, the rendered draft shows a placeholder entry for that reference.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

pulls.title: Drop trailing boxes; boxes after a segment's last mdat are not carried
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Reverts a3e3255 (the "Trailing boxes" subsection and the third rawBoxes use), which came after -01, so no published text changes.

## Why

A box after a segment's last `mdat` is ambiguous:

- CMAF describes extra boxes only before a chunk (ISO/IEC 23000-19, 7.3.2.3 Table 7 and 7.3.2.4).
- A segment's `styp` is its first box. So a box between one segment's last `mdat` and the next segment's `styp` belongs to neither segment.
- A reader that doesn't see the segment boundary takes the box as one before the next chunk.

The locmaf tools showed this concretely. On a file with a `uuid` box after segment 1's last `mdat`, `pack` (one group for the whole file) made it a genBox of segment 2's first chunk, ahead of its `styp`. `align` (one group per segment) made it a trailing rawBoxes Object of segment 1.

## What replaces it

The motivating case was a signature over the whole segment, such as a C2PA `uuid` box. It can sit before the `moof` of the segment's last chunk, where it is an ordinary genBox; only the last chunk then waits for the signature. C2PA (1.0) already places its auxiliary `uuid` box immediately before the `moof`.

One paragraph in the genBox "Ordering" subsection now says that LOCMAF does not carry a box after a segment's last `mdat`, and where to put a segment-wide box instead.

No wire change. In Eyevinn/locmaf, the implementation PR (Eyevinn/locmaf#14) is closed unmerged. A follow-up makes `pack` and `align` reject such boxes instead of silently dropping them.

pulls.title: Carry a chunk with boxes between moof and mdat verbatim
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Closes #8.

## Change

- **genBox, Ordering:** a new paragraph says that a chunk with boxes between its `moof` and its `mdat` does not fit the moof-carrying shape, because there the `mdat` immediately follows the `moof`. A publisher **MUST** carry such a chunk as a rawBoxes Object holding the whole chunk, including any boxes before its `moof`. It **MUST NOT** move the boxes before the `moof` as genBoxes: that would change the chunk's bytes and its `data_offset`, and give one chunk two encodings for canonical comparison. As after any rawBoxes Object, the next moof-carrying Object of the group is a full header.
- **rawBoxes, Verbatim chunk carriage:** this use now names the case as well.
- **genBox intro and Box carriage:** these said a genBox carries every box *outside* the `moof`. They now say every box that *precedes* the `moof`, which is what the moof-carrying shape can render.

Such boxes are outside the CMAF chunk structure (ISO/IEC 23000-19, 7.3.2.3 Table 7, where `mdat` *should* immediately follow the `trun`), but ISO BMFF allows them, since `data_offset` can skip them.

No wire change. The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`.

## Implementation

Eyevinn/locmaf cannot produce such Objects yet. mp4ff v0.62.0 refuses to parse a fragmented file with a box between `moof` and `mdat`, so `locmaf pack` and `align` reject the input. Supporting it needs mp4ff to accept these boxes and attach them to the fragment, and `pack` to emit a rawBoxes Object for such a chunk.

pulls.title: Give a CMAF video track one canonical trun version; LOCMAF 0.4
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Closes #7.

## Change

- **Canonical Reconstruction, trun:** `trun.version = 1` iff any effective composition-time offset is negative, **or** the track is video (`hdlr` handler type `vide`) and its CMAF Header has no EditListBox. Otherwise 0. New text explains why:
  - CMAF (ISO/IEC 23000-19:2024, 9.2.5) gives a video track two forms, not both: (a) version 1 TrackRunBoxes whose offsets make each fragment's earliest presentation time equal its `baseMediaDecodeTime` (see also 7.5.17), or (b) an offset edit list in the CMAF Header with version 0 TrackRunBoxes.
  - Under the old per-chunk rule, a form (a) track was rebuilt with version 0 in every chunk without a negative offset. That includes chunks without B-frames and short chunks whose offsets are all non-negative. Such a chunk fits neither form.
  - Video without an edit list gets version 1 in every chunk. Video with an edit list gets version 0, and version 1 only in a chunk with a negative offset, which is a non-conformant source but keeps its timing. Audio, subtitles and metadata are unchanged.
  - Only the presence of an EditListBox matters, since 7.5.13 allows only an offset edit list in a CMAF Header. Timing is unchanged: a non-negative offset has the same meaning in both versions.
- **Canonical Reconstruction, Effective values:** the CMAF Header inputs now include the `hdlr` handler type and whether the `trak` has an EditListBox.
- **Catalog Signaling:** the LOCMAF version is now `0.4` (`"packagingMetadata": "version=0.4"`). The paragraph on what the `version` key signals now also covers changes to the canonical reconstruction, since conformance compares its bytes exactly.

The wire format does not change, but the canonical bytes of most video chunks do. Two implementations of the old and new rule would disagree byte for byte while both claiming 0.3, hence the bump. The published -01 cut specified 0.3, so the next cut is the first with 0.4.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`. `make check` reports only the expected nits.

## Follow-up

Eyevinn/locmaf: `computeLayout` in `reconstruct.go`, the `align` explainer, new vector cases (a video chunk without negative offsets, and a video track with an edit list), regenerated vectors, and `locmaf.Version` 0.4. Then the 0.4 pins in moqlivemock, msf-catalog-validator and locmaf.dev.

pulls.title: Add a Change Log appendix listing the changes since -01
pulls.author: tobbee
pulls.body:
Adds **Appendix A, Change Log**, ahead of the -02 cut. It is marked `removeinrfc`, so it renders with the "to be removed before publishing as an RFC" note. It has one subsection per cut, starting with **Since draft-einarsson-moq-locmaf-01**, and each item points to its section.

## Contents

- **Changes that affect implementations**
  - LOCMAF packaging version 0.4.
  - The version is a `version` key in MSF `packagingMetadata`, replacing the `locmafVersion` track field; CMSF registers `locmaf`.
  - `mfhdSequenceNumber` (ID 18) and `mfhdSequenceNumberStep` (ID 20), so the canonical `mfhd` no longer always carries 0.
  - Canonical `trun` version 1 in every chunk of a video track without an edit list (#7).
  - A chunk with boxes between `moof` and `mdat` is carried as rawBoxes (#8); a box after a segment's last `mdat` is not carried.
- **Clarifications:** the extensibility rule (decode-equivalent is enough, even if canonical bytes differ), and that a genBox carries the boxes before the `moof`.
- **Editorial:** Related Work, updated references, corrected CMAF clause numbers.

The trailing-boxes change (a3e3255) and its revert (bb4c68e) both came after -01 and cancel out, so only the resulting rule is listed.

The draft renders, stays within 72 columns, and passes `make lint`. `make check` reports only the expected nits, plus the two broken references below.

## Before submitting -02

`draft-ietf-moq-msf-02` and `draft-ietf-moq-cmsf-02` are not on the Datatracker yet: their bibxml returns 404, and every build inserts broken references for them. Submit -02 only after both are published.
